How long these wars lasted.Third Punic War: Rome razed Carthage in 146 BC; the story that the Romans sowed the ground with salt is most likely a later myth.
How long these wars lasted.Caesar's Gallic Wars: Caesar wrote his own account of the campaign, starting with the famous line that all Gaul is divided into three parts.
How long these wars lasted.Second Punic War: Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Italy, and Scipio finally defeated him at Zama in North Africa.
How long these wars lasted.Peloponnesian War: Athens and Sparta fought it, and the historian Thucydides, who lived through it, wrote an account that is still read in military academies.
How long these wars lasted.Wars of the Roses: The name comes from the emblems of the houses of York and Lancaster, and the war ended with Henry Tudor taking the throne.
How long these wars lasted.Greco-Persian Wars: Greece and Persia clashed in battles at Marathon, Thermopylae and Salamis, whose stories came to us largely from Herodotus.
How long these wars lasted.Mongol conquest of China: Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty at its end, after generations of Mongol campaigns that overwhelmed the Song dynasty.
How long these wars lasted.Hundred Years' War: The name is a convenient label for what was really many on-and-off conflicts, and Joan of Arc rose to fame during it.
How long these wars lasted.Crusades to the Holy Land: These expeditions started in 1095 with a call from Pope Urban II and ended with the fall of Acre in 1291.
How long these wars lasted.Reconquista: It ended in 1492, the year Columbus sailed, with the fall of Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Iberia.

Space stations through the years.Salyut 1 launches: The USSR launched the first space station in 1971; its first crew died when a valve opened during their return in Soyuz 11.
Space stations through the years.Skylab launches: Built from a spare Saturn V rocket stage, it fell back to Earth in 1979 and scattered debris across western Australia.
Space stations through the years.Mir core module launches: The Soviet, then Russian, station stayed in orbit for 15 years and was deliberately brought down over the Pacific in 2001.
Space stations through the years.ISS's first module, Zarya: Russian-built but paid for by NASA, its name means Dawn, and it was the first piece of the International Space Station.
Space stations through the years.First ISS crew arrives: Expedition 1 arrived on 2 November 2000; humans have lived aboard the ISS continuously ever since.
Space stations through the years.Tiangong-1 launches: China's first space lab, whose name means Heavenly Palace, fell out of control in 2018 and mostly burned up over the South Pacific.
Space stations through the years.First Dragon cargo berthing: In May 2012 SpaceX's Dragon became the first commercial spacecraft to deliver cargo to the ISS.
Space stations through the years.Tiangong-2 launches: China's second space lab hosted two astronauts for about a month in 2016 and was deliberately brought down in 2019.
Space stations through the years.Crew Dragon's first crew: Demo-2 in May 2020 was the first crewed orbital launch from US soil since the Space Shuttle retired in 2011.
Space stations through the years.Tianhe core module launches: Its name means Harmony of the Heavens; it is the core of China's three-module Tiangong station.

Big moments of the long 19th century.Battle of Trafalgar: Nelson was killed in the battle; his flagship was HMS Victory, still preserved at Portsmouth.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Battle of Waterloo: Napoleon's final defeat, by Wellington and Blucher in what is now Belgium, gave us the phrase meet your Waterloo.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Victoria becomes queen: She was 18 when she became queen in 1837, and reigned for over 63 years.
Big moments of the long 19th century.California Gold Rush: Gold found at Sutter's Mill in January 1848 drew about 300,000 people to California.
Big moments of the long 19th century.US Civil War begins: It began with the attack on Fort Sumter in April 1861.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Germany unifies: The German Empire was proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles in January 1871.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Statue of Liberty dedicated: A gift from France, dedicated in October 1886, its copper skin has turned green.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Eiffel Tower opens: Built for the 1889 World's Fair, it was meant to stand for only 20 years.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Spanish-American War: It made the US a colonial power, gaining Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
Big moments of the long 19th century.Queen Victoria dies: She died in January 1901, and her reign was the longest in British history until Elizabeth II surpassed it.

Ridley Scott films by release.The Duellists: Scott's debut feature, based on a Joseph Conrad story, follows two officers dueling on and off for years, and won a Cannes prize.
Ridley Scott films by release.Alien: Its tagline, 'In space no one can hear you scream', and H. R. Giger's creature design made it a horror and sci-fi classic.
Ridley Scott films by release.Blade Runner: Based on a Philip K. Dick novel, it exists in several different cuts, and it flopped at first before becoming a cult classic.
Ridley Scott films by release.Thelma & Louise: Callie Khouri won the Oscar for her screenplay, and Brad Pitt had his breakout role in this road movie.
Ridley Scott films by release.Gladiator: It won Best Picture and Best Actor for Russell Crowe, reviving the sword-and-sandal epic.
Ridley Scott films by release.Black Hawk Down: It follows the 1993 battle in Mogadishu and won Oscars for editing and sound.
Ridley Scott films by release.Kingdom of Heaven: The Crusades epic was a disappointment on release, but a longer director's cut earned far better reviews.
Ridley Scott films by release.Prometheus: Its title borrows from the Greek Titan who stole fire from the gods, and it serves as a prequel to Alien.
Ridley Scott films by release.The Martian: Based on Andy Weir's novel, which began as a self-published online serial, and filmed partly in Jordan's Wadi Rum desert.
Ridley Scott films by release.Napoleon: Joaquin Phoenix plays the emperor, and Scott's staging of the Battle of Austerlitz includes a frozen-lake sequence.

Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Aleph: A silent letter, it is the ancestor of the Greek alpha and the Latin A.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Gimel: The name means camel, and the letter is the ancestor of the Greek gamma and the Latin C and G.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Dalet: Its name means door, and the letter is the ancestor of the Greek delta.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Vav: It means hook, and as a one-letter prefix it also means and.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Yod: The smallest letter in the alphabet is the ancestor of the Greek iota and the Latin I.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Lamed: Its tall ascender makes it the tallest Hebrew letter, and the name is linked to an ox goad.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Mem: Probably descended from a wavy symbol for water, it is the ancestor of the Greek mu and Latin M.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Samekh: Its name means support, and its round shape is one of the simplest in the alphabet.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Resh: Its name means head, and through the Greek rho it gave us the Latin letter R.
Letters of the Hebrew alphabet.Tav: The last letter, its name means mark, and it is the ancestor of the Greek tau and the Latin T.

Literary magazines, by founding year.Punch: This British satirical weekly gave us the modern sense of the word cartoon in 1843, and it closed in 2002.
Literary magazines, by founding year.Harper's Magazine: Founded by the Harper brothers, it is the oldest continuously published monthly magazine in America.
Literary magazines, by founding year.The Atlantic: Launched in Boston with Emerson and Longfellow among its founders, it published Julia Ward Howe's Battle Hymn of the Republic.
Literary magazines, by founding year.Granta: Founded by Cambridge students, it was relaunched in 1979 and made its name with themed issues such as Best of Young British Novelists.
Literary magazines, by founding year.The Strand Magazine: It serialised Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes stories, with Sidney Paget's illustrations shaping how Holmes looked.
Literary magazines, by founding year.Times Literary Supplement: Started as a supplement to The Times, it grew into an independent weekly of book reviews whose reviewers stayed anonymous until 1974.
Literary magazines, by founding year.Poetry (Chicago): Founded by Harriet Monroe, it first printed T. S. Eliot's The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock in 1915.
Literary magazines, by founding year.The New Yorker: Its mascot Eustace Tilley, a dandy peering at a butterfly through a monocle, appeared on the first cover and returns every anniversary.
Literary magazines, by founding year.The Paris Review: Famed for its Art of Fiction interviews with writers, it was founded in Paris by Peter Matthiessen, George Plimpton and others.
Literary magazines, by founding year.The New York Review of Books: It began during a New York newspaper strike, when editors hurriedly assembled the first issue of book reviews.

HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Continue: A server sends 100 so a client can confirm it will accept a large request body before sending it.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.OK: The most-seen success code means the request worked and the response carries what you asked for.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Created: Servers return this after a new resource is made, such as a freshly submitted account or post.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.No Content: It means success with nothing to send back, handy for deleting something or saving without reloading a page.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Moved Permanently: This code tells browsers and search engines a page has a new address for good.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Not Modified: It saves bandwidth by telling the browser that its cached copy is still current, so nothing is downloaded again.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Forbidden: This means the server understood but refuses; unlike 401, signing in won't necessarily help.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Not Found: The web's best-known error means the page is missing, and the tale of a room at CERN behind its name is a myth.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.I'm a teapot: A 1998 April Fools' RFC defined a Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol, and a teapot cannot brew coffee.
HTTP status messages by their code numbe.Service Unavailable: It means the server is overloaded or down for maintenance, and it can tell clients when to retry.

When these London rail lines first opene.Metropolitan line: The world's first underground passenger railway opened in 1863 between Paddington and Farringdon, hauled by steam locomotives.
When these London rail lines first opene.District line: It was built to complete the inner circle route, which was joined with the Metropolitan in 1884 to form the Circle line.
When these London rail lines first opene.Northern line (first section): The City & South London Railway was the first deep-level electric tube, running from Stockwell to King William Street.
When these London rail lines first opene.Waterloo & City line: Nicknamed 'the Drain', it links just two stations, Waterloo and Bank, and is built for commuters.
When these London rail lines first opene.Central line: Nicknamed the Twopenny Tube, it charged a flat fare of just twopence when it opened in 1900.
When these London rail lines first opene.Bakerloo line: The name joins Baker Street and Waterloo; a newspaper coined 'Bakerloo' and the name stuck.
When these London rail lines first opene.Victoria line: It was the first line to use fully automatic train operation, with drivers only closing the doors.
When these London rail lines first opene.Jubilee line: It was planned as the Fleet line, then renamed for the Queen's Silver Jubilee of 1977 before opening.
When these London rail lines first opene.Docklands Light Railway: Its driverless trains have staff called 'train captains', and it was built to regenerate the old docklands.
When these London rail lines first opene.Elizabeth line: Named for the late Queen, it opened in May 2022 after the Crossrail project, whose tunnelling machines were given names like Phyllis and Ada.

When these ancient disasters struck.Thera (Santorini) erupts: One of the largest eruptions in human history; it may have crippled the Minoans and inspired the legend of Atlantis.
When these ancient disasters struck.Plague of Athens: It killed perhaps a third of the city, including its leader Pericles, and Thucydides described it, having survived it himself.
When these ancient disasters struck.Earthquake topples Colossus: The Colossus of Rhodes stood only about 54 years before it fell.
When these ancient disasters struck.Great Fire of Rome: Nero was said to fiddle while Rome burned, though he played a lyre, and he blamed Christians for it.
When these ancient disasters struck.Vesuvius buries Pompeii: Ash preserved the town of Pompeii, down to bread still in the ovens.
When these ancient disasters struck.Antonine Plague begins: Probably smallpox, brought home by soldiers, and it killed millions across the Roman Empire.
When these ancient disasters struck.Crete quake and tsunami: The quake and tsunami hit Alexandria, stranding ships far inland.
When these ancient disasters struck.Plague of Justinian: The first recorded pandemic of bubonic plague began in the reign of the Byzantine emperor Justinian.
When these ancient disasters struck.Samalas volcano erupts: This volcano in Indonesia was a mystery until researchers traced its ash in ice cores, and it cooled the global climate.
When these ancient disasters struck.Black Death hits Europe: The plague killed perhaps a third to half of Europe's people.

Shapes by lines of symmetry.Scalene triangle: Every side and angle differs, so no fold maps it onto itself, unlike an isosceles triangle, which has one line.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Letter A: Many capital letters, such as A, M, T, U, V and W, share its single vertical line of symmetry, so they look the same in a mirror.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Rectangle: A common mistake: a rectangle's diagonals are not lines of symmetry, only the two midlines are, unless it is a square.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Equilateral triangle: Each line runs from a corner to the middle of the opposite side, and the triangle also has three-fold rotational symmetry.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Square: A square has two diagonal lines and two lines through the midpoints of opposite sides, making it the most symmetric four-sided shape.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Regular pentagon: Each line passes through a vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side, so every line has one corner on it.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Regular hexagon: Bees build hexagon cells, which tile a flat surface with the least wax, and the shape's six lines give it plenty of symmetry.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Stop sign: The octagon was chosen so drivers can recognize the sign even from behind, or when it is covered in snow.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Regular decagon: Each interior angle is 144 degrees, and its ten lines are half through vertices, half through the midpoints of sides.
Shapes by lines of symmetry.Regular dodecagon: The British pound coin since 2017 has twelve sides, partly to make it harder to counterfeit, and so it has twelve symmetry lines.

American football's famous moments.The Ice Bowl: The 1967 NFL title game in Green Bay, in bitter cold of about minus 13 degrees Fahrenheit, ended with a quarterback sneak.
American football's famous moments.Monday Night Football debuts: This weekly prime-time broadcast started in September 1970 and became a TV institution.
American football's famous moments.The Immaculate Reception: Franco Harris caught a deflected pass and ran for a touchdown to beat the Raiders.
American football's famous moments.The Catch: Dwight Clark's leaping grab from Joe Montana beat the Cowboys in the 1982 NFC title game.
American football's famous moments.Flutie's Hail Mary: Boston College quarterback Doug Flutie threw a last-second pass to beat Miami 47-45.
American football's famous moments.Music City Miracle: A trick lateral on the kickoff helped the Titans beat the Bills in a playoff game.
American football's famous moments.The Helmet Catch: David Tyree pinned the ball against his helmet as the Giants upset the unbeaten Patriots in the Super Bowl.
American football's famous moments.Malcolm Butler's interception: The Seahawks threw from the one-yard line, and Butler's goal-line pick sealed the Super Bowl for the Patriots.
American football's famous moments.Patriots' 28-3 comeback: The Patriots trailed 28-3 to the Falcons in Super Bowl LI and won in the first overtime in the game's history.
American football's famous moments.The Philly Special: In the Super Bowl, quarterback Nick Foles caught a touchdown pass in a trick play.

When these chemical elements were discov.Phosphorus: Hennig Brand discovered it by boiling down urine, and the glowing element lights up on exposure to air.
When these chemical elements were discov.Hydrogen: Henry Cavendish isolated it and called it 'inflammable air'.
When these chemical elements were discov.Oxygen: Priestley, Scheele and Lavoisier all have claims to its discovery.
When these chemical elements were discov.Uranium: Martin Klaproth named it for Uranus, discovered just eight years earlier.
When these chemical elements were discov.Sodium: Humphry Davy isolated it by electrolysis, producing a metal that explodes in water.
When these chemical elements were discov.Helium: First seen in the Sun's spectrum in an eclipse, it is named for the Greek god Helios.
When these chemical elements were discov.Argon: Its name means 'lazy' in Greek, because it barely reacts with anything.
When these chemical elements were discov.Radium: Marie and Pierre Curie discovered it, and it glows faintly in the dark.
When these chemical elements were discov.Plutonium: Glenn Seaborg's team at Berkeley made it, naming it after Pluto.
When these chemical elements were discov.Promethium: It is the last of the rare-earth elements to be found, named for the Titan Prometheus.

Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Latin: It has no native speakers but is still used in the Vatican, and the Romance languages are its descendants.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Navajo: Navajo speakers served as WWII code talkers, and the code was never broken.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Basque: A language isolate: it has no known relatives anywhere in the world.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Slovenian: It has a dual grammatical number for exactly two of something.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Finnish: It has about 15 noun cases and is not related to most European languages.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Hungarian: Hungarians put their family name first, as in East Asia; its closest relatives include Finnish.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Polish: It is known for consonant clusters; 'chrzaszcz', meaning beetle, is a famous tongue-twister.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Korean: King Sejong had the Hangul alphabet created in 1443, designed to be easy to learn.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.Bengali: The 1952 Language Movement in Bangladesh led UNESCO to proclaim 21 February International Mother Language Day.
Native speakers, from none at all to glo.English: More people speak it as a second language than natives, making it the most widely spoken language overall.

Great rivers of the world by length.Liffey: James Joyce used its Dublin banks as a character, 'Anna Livia', in Finnegans Wake.
Great rivers of the world by length.Shannon: Ireland's longest river, it empties into the Atlantic and powers a hydroelectric plant.
Great rivers of the world by length.Orinoco: Venezuela's great river; Angel Falls, the world's tallest waterfall, is in its basin.
Great rivers of the world by length.Zambezi: It spills over Victoria Falls, called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'.
Great rivers of the world by length.Yukon: Prospectors travelled along it during the Klondike Gold Rush; it ends in the Bering Sea.
Great rivers of the world by length.Mississippi: Its tributary, the Missouri, is actually longer, so together they make the longest US river system.
Great rivers of the world by length.Niger: It flows away from the sea first, in a boomerang shape, before turning south.
Great rivers of the world by length.Congo: The deepest river on Earth, plunging over 200 metres in places.
Great rivers of the world by length.Yangtze: Asia's longest river, home to the Three Gorges Dam.
Great rivers of the world by length.Nile: It flows north, and Egyptian civilization grew from its floods; its length is disputed with the Amazon.

Scrabble face value of these foods.Tea: It is the world's most consumed drink after water, and many languages derive the word from te or cha.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Egg: Its shell has thousands of tiny pores, and its color depends on the hen's breed.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Lemon: Sailors fought scurvy with this fruit or limes, rich in vitamin C.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Burrito: The name means little donkey in Spanish.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Jam: Jam has fruit pieces, unlike jelly, and sets thanks to the pectin in the fruit.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Falafel: This Middle Eastern snack is made from chickpeas, or from fava beans in Egypt.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Quinoa: It is not a true grain but a seed, and the Incas called it the mother grain.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Squash: It is one of the Three Sisters of Native American farming, grown with corn and beans.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Quiche: The name comes from the German Kuchen, cake, and the dish comes from Lorraine.
Scrabble face value of these foods.Jambalaya: Louisiana's rice dish mixes French and Spanish influences, similar to paella.

Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Cupcake: Android's dessert naming began with this release in 2009; the earliest versions had no names.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Donut: It added a search feature and support for varied screen sizes.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Eclair: It brought turn-by-turn Google Maps Navigation, launched on the Motorola Droid.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Froyo: Short for 'frozen yogurt', it added the ability to share a phone's connection as a Wi-Fi hotspot.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Gingerbread: It added support for NFC, the tech behind contactless phone payments, and ran on phones for years.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Honeycomb: The tablet-only release launched on the Motorola Xoom, and phones never got it.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Ice Cream Sandwich: It merged phone and tablet versions, introducing the Roboto font and Face Unlock.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Jelly Bean: Called 'Project Butter', it made the interface smoother at 60 frames a second and introduced Google Now.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.KitKat: Google partnered with Nestlé for the name, having considered 'Key Lime Pie'.
Android's sweet codenames, in version or.Lollipop: Material Design arrived with this release, redefining how Android apps look.

Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Septuagesima Sunday: The name means 'seventieth' in Latin, though it falls 63 days before Easter. It began the pre-Lent season until dropped in 1969.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Shrove Tuesday: 'Shrove' comes from shrive, to confess. Rich foods were used up in pancakes before Lent, hence Mardi Gras, French for Fat Tuesday.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Ash Wednesday: Opens Lent. The ashes used are traditionally made by burning the palm fronds saved from the previous year's Palm Sunday.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Palm Sunday: Recalls Jesus entering Jerusalem as crowds laid palm branches before him. It starts Holy Week.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Maundy Thursday: 'Maundy' comes from the Latin for commandment. On this day the British monarch hands out specially minted Maundy money.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Good Friday: Commemorates the crucifixion. The 'good' here likely meant holy, and it is a public holiday in many countries.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Easter Sunday: Its date is the first Sunday after the first full moon on or after the spring equinox, so it ranges from 22 March to 25 April.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Ascension Day: Always falls on a Thursday and marks Jesus rising to heaven. It is a public holiday in countries such as Germany and France.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Pentecost: The name comes from the Greek for fiftieth. In Britain it is also Whitsun, probably from 'White Sunday', for baptismal robes.
Moveable feasts, measured from Easter Su.Corpus Christi: Latin for 'body of Christ'. It is always a Thursday, and a Cambridge college and a Texas city are named after it.

Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Leafcutter ant: Leafcutter ants don't eat the leaves they carry; they use them to grow a fungus garden that feeds the whole colony.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Strawberry poison frog: The bright colors warn of toxins in its skin, and this frog's tadpoles are carried on the parent's back to tiny pools of water.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Vampire bat: These bats share blood meals by regurgitating to roostmates who failed to feed, since a bat can starve in about two days.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Scarlet macaw: Macaws gather at riverbank clay licks to eat soil that helps neutralize toxins in the seeds they eat.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Three-toed sloth: Its slow metabolism means it climbs down only about once a week, to the forest floor, to relieve itself, and moths live in its fur.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Harpy eagle (female): Its talons are about as long as a grizzly's claws, which it uses to snatch sloths and monkeys right from the canopy.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Giant otter: Living in noisy family groups, these giant otters can reach up to 1.8 m long and are nicknamed river wolves.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Capybara: The world's largest rodent, it spends much of its time in water and is happy to let birds sit on its back.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.Jaguar: With the strongest bite among big cats for its size, it can crack turtle shells and even caiman hides.
Amazon rainforest animals by weight.South American tapir: Related to horses and rhinos, it has a short flexible snout, and its babies are born with spots and stripes.

Art movements, by when they began.Baroque: The name probably comes from a Portuguese word for an irregular pearl, and Caravaggio's dramatic light defined the style.
Art movements, by when they began.Rococo: It takes its name from rocaille, shell-like ornament, and favoured lighter, playful scenes such as Fragonard's The Swing.
Art movements, by when they began.Neoclassicism: It was a reaction to ornate styles, inspired partly by the excavations of Pompeii and Herculaneum, and David's Oath of the Horatii is typical.
Art movements, by when they began.Romanticism: It celebrated emotion and wild nature, and Frankenstein was written by one of its writers in 1818.
Art movements, by when they began.Impressionism: A critic mocked Monet's painting 'Impression, Sunrise', and the artists adopted the insult as their name.
Art movements, by when they began.Cubism: Picasso and Braque broke objects into geometric facets, and a critic's jibe about 'little cubes' gave it its name.
Art movements, by when they began.Futurism: Marinetti's 1909 manifesto in Le Figaro celebrated speed, machines and violence, and rejected the past.
Art movements, by when they began.Dada: Born at the Cabaret Voltaire in Zurich in response to World War I, it mocked logic and led to Duchamp's urinal.
Art movements, by when they began.Surrealism: Andre Breton's 1924 manifesto launched it, and Dali and Magritte turned dreams into painting.
Art movements, by when they began.Pop Art: It began in Britain with Richard Hamilton's 1956 collage, and then boomed with Warhol's soup cans in America.

Video game movies by release year.Super Mario Bros. (film): Starring Bob Hoskins as Mario, it flopped, and he later called it the worst thing he ever did.
Video game movies by release year.Street Fighter: Raúl Juliá played villain M. Bison in his final film role; he died shortly before its release.
Video game movies by release year.Mortal Kombat: Its techno theme 'Techno Syndrome' made it a cult hit, and fans still chant 'Mortal Kombat!' along with it.
Video game movies by release year.Lara Croft: Tomb Raider: Angelina Jolie did many of her own stunts, and the temple scenes were shot at Ta Prohm in Cambodia.
Video game movies by release year.Resident Evil: The heroine Alice was invented for the movies and never appeared in the games; the franchise ran to six films.
Video game movies by release year.Doom: Dwayne Johnson starred, and the film included a first-person shooter sequence mimicking the game's point of view.
Video game movies by release year.Prince of Persia: The 1989 game's lifelike animation was rotoscoped from footage of creator Jordan Mechner's younger brother.
Video game movies by release year.Warcraft: Blizzard's orcs-versus-humans epic earned over $400 million worldwide, with more than half coming from China.
Video game movies by release year.Detective Pikachu: Ryan Reynolds voiced the talking Pikachu, and it was the first live-action Pokémon film, earning over $400 million.
Video game movies by release year.A Minecraft Movie: A line about a 'chicken jockey' sent audiences into popcorn-throwing frenzy, and it grossed over $900 million worldwide.

Famous novels, by number of chapters.The Great Gatsby: The Great Gatsby is only nine chapters long, and Fitzgerald's slim novel is often called the great American novel.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Alice in Wonderland: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland has twelve chapters, and Lewis Carroll first told the tale on a boat trip.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Harry Potter (book 1): Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone has 17 chapters, and it was rejected by a dozen publishers before being accepted.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Ulysses: Ulysses has 18 episodes, matching the Odyssey, and it's set on a single day, June 16, 1904.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.The Hobbit: The Hobbit has 19 chapters, and Tolkien famously began it by scribbling a line on an exam paper.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Dracula: Dracula has 27 chapters, and it's told through letters, diaries and news clippings.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Jane Eyre: Jane Eyre has 38 chapters, and Charlotte Bronte first published it under the male pseudonym Currer Bell.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Pride and Prejudice: Pride and Prejudice has 61 chapters, and it was first titled First Impressions.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Don Quixote (both parts): Don Quixote is often called the first modern novel, and the windmill episode gave us tilting at windmills.
Famous novels, by number of chapters.Moby-Dick: Moby-Dick has 135 chapters and an epilogue, and it was a commercial flop in Melville's lifetime.

Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Non-alcoholic beer: Even 'non-alcoholic' beer may legally contain up to 0.5 percent, about what ripe fruit or bread can contain.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Typical lager: Lager yeast works slowly in the cold; the word means 'storage' in German, for the months beer was cellared.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Red wine: A typical bottle contains 12 to 15 percent, and grapes from warmer climates ripen sweeter, giving stronger wine.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Baileys Irish Cream: Launched in 1974, it blends Irish whiskey and cream, and was among the first cream liqueurs.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Port: Port is fortified with brandy, which halts fermentation and leaves natural sweetness; it comes from Portugal's Douro Valley.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Jägermeister: This German herbal liqueur uses 56 herbs and spices, and its stag-and-cross label refers to St Hubertus, patron of hunters.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Standard vodka: The 40 percent standard is 80 proof in the US; 'proof' comes from an old test where gunpowder soaked in spirit would still burn.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Navy-strength gin: By tradition, navy-strength gin is at least 57 percent, strong enough that gunpowder soaked in it would still ignite.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Bacardi 151: Its 151 refers to proof, which is 75.5 percent alcohol, and it was discontinued in the US in 2016, mainly over safety concerns.
Alcohol by volume: from barely to brutal.Everclear (strongest): This 190-proof grain spirit is banned in several US states and is often used to make extracts and tinctures.

Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.egy: Hungarian is unrelated to its Indo-European neighbors; it belongs to the Uralic family, with Finnish and Estonian.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.kettő: Two has a short form, 'két', used before nouns, as in 'két kutya', two dogs.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.három: Nouns stay singular after numbers, so it is 'három kutya', literally 'three dog'.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.négy: The letters 'gy' stand for one sound, like a soft 'dy', so it sounds roughly like 'nedj'.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.öt: The word is distantly related to Finnish 'viisi' and Estonian 'viis' through the Uralic family.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.hat: The word is distantly related to Finnish 'kuusi', another sign of the shared Uralic roots.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.hét: 'Hét' means both seven and week, since a week has seven days.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.nyolc: The 'ny' pair makes one sound, like the 'ni' in onion, so it is said roughly 'nyolts'.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.kilenc: The 'c' sounds like 'ts', so it is said roughly 'KEE-lents'.
Hungarian numbers, by the value they nam.tíz: Eleven is 'tizenegy', which literally means 'ten on one', so teens are built from this word.

Odd units of length.Beard-second: A physicist's joke measure: how far a beard grows in one second, about five nanometers, a handful of atoms.
Odd units of length.Thou (mil): One thousandth of an inch, and a favorite unit of machinists measuring tight tolerances.
Odd units of length.Mickey: The smallest movement a computer mouse can detect, about 1/200 of an inch, a unit used by programmers.
Odd units of length.Hand: Used to measure horses' height; one hand is four inches, and a horse is measured to its withers.
Odd units of length.Banana for scale: A banana for scale is an internet joke for comparing sizes, though a real banana varies between 15 and 20 cm.
Odd units of length.Smoot: MIT students rolled Oliver Smoot across the Harvard Bridge in 1958 and marked its length in smoots, and the paint is still refreshed.
Odd units of length.Double-decker bus: A double-decker bus is roughly 11 m long, and most London buses fit about this size.
Odd units of length.Olympic pool: The 50 m length is standard for Olympic competition, and the pool is at least two meters deep.
Odd units of length.American football field: The playing field is 100 yards between goal lines, with end zones adding ten yards each side.
Odd units of length.Sheppey: A whimsical, unofficial unit said to be the distance at which a sheep remains picturesque.

Teen movies by release.Rebel Without a Cause: James Dean died in a car crash a month before it opened, so he never saw his iconic performance become a cultural landmark.
Teen movies by release.American Graffiti: Set over a single night in 1962, it was made for under $1 million and became one of the most profitable films ever.
Teen movies by release.Fast Times at Ridgemont High: Cameron Crowe went undercover at a San Diego high school to write the book it's based on; the cast includes Sean Penn and a young Nicolas Cage.
Teen movies by release.The Breakfast Club: Most of it takes place in a school library, a set built in a gym of a closed Illinois high school.
Teen movies by release.Ferris Bueller's Day Off: The red Ferrari in the film was a replica, because the real 1961 model was far too valuable to wreck.
Teen movies by release.10 Things I Hate About You: A modern retelling of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, filmed in Tacoma, it made Heath Ledger a star in Hollywood.
Teen movies by release.Napoleon Dynamite: Made for about $400,000, it grew from director Jared Hess's short film and earned many times that at the box office.
Teen movies by release.Juno: Diablo Cody's first screenplay won her an Oscar, and its quirky soundtrack, led by Kimya Dawson, became a hit in its own right.
Teen movies by release.Easy A: It loosely updates Hawthorne's The Scarlet Letter, and it gave Emma Stone her first starring role.
Teen movies by release.Lady Bird: Greta Gerwig's first solo directorial effort, set in Sacramento, earned Oscar nominations for Best Picture and Best Director.

When these famous duets came out.Somethin' Stupid: Frank Sinatra sang it with his daughter Nancy, a father-daughter duet that topped charts on both sides of the Atlantic.
When these famous duets came out.Don't Go Breaking My Heart: It gave Elton John his first UK number one, a playful tribute to Motown duets.
When these famous duets came out.Endless Love: Written by Lionel Richie for a film of the same name, it became one of Motown's biggest-selling singles.
When these famous duets came out.Islands in the Stream: Written by the Bee Gees' Gibb brothers, it was originally meant for Marvin Gaye before Dolly and Kenny took it.
When these famous duets came out.(I've Had) The Time of My Life: From Dirty Dancing, it won an Oscar and a Grammy for Bill Medley and Jennifer Warnes.
When these famous duets came out.Empire State of Mind: This tribute to New York was written in part by the artists themselves, and its piano hook became a fixture at Yankees games.
When these famous duets came out.Shallow: From A Star Is Born, it won an Oscar for Best Original Song.
When these famous duets came out.Señorita: It topped the charts in several countries and mixes English with a Spanish title.
When these famous duets came out.Die with a Smile: Gaga and Bruno Mars released it in August 2024, and it won a Grammy for best pop duo or group performance.

Shrek, in story order.Shrek meets Donkey: Eddie Murphy voices Donkey, while Mike Myers famously re-recorded Shrek with a Scottish accent.
Shrek, in story order.Squatters fill Shrek's swamp: Fairy-tale creatures like Pinocchio, the Three Little Pigs and Gingy end up in the swamp after Farquaad kicks them out.
Shrek, in story order.Farquaad's tournament: Shrek (2001) won the very first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.
Shrek, in story order.Rescuing Fiona from the dragon: The dragon is female, nicknamed Dragon, and falls for Donkey, a twist on the usual dragon story.
Shrek, in story order.Fiona fights Robin Hood: Fiona's fight with Robin Hood parodies The Matrix's slow-motion bullet-time.
Shrek, in story order.Donkey learns Fiona's secret: Fiona's nightly transformation subverts fairy tales where a curse is broken by love's first kiss.
Shrek, in story order.Shrek storms off: Smash Mouth's All Star plays over the opening, and became forever tied to the film.
Shrek, in story order.Shrek objects at the wedding: The wedding interruption parodies romantic comedies, with the hero bursting in to stop it.
Shrek, in story order.Dragon eats Farquaad: Lord Farquaad is voiced by John Lithgow, and his short stature is a running joke.
Shrek, in story order.Shrek and Fiona marry: The film ends with Fiona staying an ogre, a message about accepting how you look.
